coverage.summary: Ability checks, skill checks, saving throws, the full character sheet, spell slots, hit dice, class resources, conditions, rests, and 5e combat: attack rolls against Armor Class with advantage and criticals, saves, concentration, death saves, the SRD monsters, and a fight on a board in feet with movement, reach, range, cover and areas. Not yet: chosen reactions, elevation, grapple and shove.

naturals.$comment: 2014 rules: a natural 20 or 1 decides attack rolls only. Checks and saves are pure arithmetic, unlike Marinara's own rules.

fields.$comment: SRD 5.1, Speed: "Your speed defines how far you can move when you move on your turn." A fight on a board reads this field through combat.economy.movement. It defaults to 30, which is what most SRD races walk; this sheet has no race mechanics, so a Wood Elf's 35 or a Dwarf's 25 is typed in here rather than read off anything.
fields.label: Speed (ft)

derived.$comment: Class resource maximums the SRD ties to an ability score rather than to a class table. A catalog entry's scaled column reads them, so the sheet keeps the counter it picked. They carry no section, so they sit beside the Class resources list, and no hide rule, because the sheet has no field that says which class you are and a hide rule can only compare one to a value.
derived.label: Bardic Inspiration uses

derived.$comment: Lay on Hands is a pool of hit points, not a count of uses, so it is the one class resource whose maximum is a multiple of the level.
derived.label: Lay on Hands pool

columns.$comment: How far this weapon strikes on a board, in feet. SRD 5.1 Melee Attacks: "you can attack a target within 5 feet of you", and the Reach property: "This weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it." A row that only shoots reads 0.
columns.label: Reach (ft)

columns.$comment: The ordinary distance this weapon is thrown or shot, in feet. SRD 5.1 Range: "A weapon that can be used to make a ranged attack has a range in parentheses after the ammunition or thrown property." 0 is a weapon that is neither thrown nor shot.
columns.label: Range (ft)

columns.$comment: The longer distance the same shot still carries, in feet. SRD 5.1 Range: "Your attack has disadvantage when your target is beyond normal range, and you can't attack a target beyond the long range."
columns.label: Long range (ft)

lists.$comment: Ki, Rage, Sorcery Points, Channel Divinity, Bardic Inspiration and the like, without shipping class tables. Each row is a live pool.
lists.label: Class resources

live.$comment: Fast-changing state. Starts from the build when a game copies the sheet, and lives with the game-state snapshot so a swipe rewinds it.

rests.$comment: Spending hit dice is a player choice made on the sheet; the rest itself does not spend them.
rests.label: Short rest

gm.checkGuidance: This game uses 5e rules from SRD 5.1. Call for an ability check, skill check or saving throw only when the outcome is uncertain and failure is interesting. Name the skill or the save and set a DC from the ladder below. Never add modifiers, never state a total and never decide the result: the Engine applies the character sheet and reports the outcome. A natural 20 or natural 1 has no special effect on checks or saves.
gm.sheetGuidance: The character sheets below are authoritative. A character can only cast a spell that is on their sheet and only with a slot they still have. When a character spends or regains a resource, takes damage, heals, gains or loses a condition, or rests, record it with the sheet command. If a command is refused, the fiction did not happen: narrate around it.

battle.$comment: What a battle may read from this sheet when a game is NOT fighting by the combat block below. It is not a 5e combat adapter: there are no attack rolls, no saving throws and no concentration on this path, and the damage arithmetic stays Marinara's. Hit points, slots and the spells and attacks a player picked from a catalog are simply lent to Marinara's own combat. Pact Magic slots are left out, because their level follows the character's own level and a fixed list of levels cannot say that. This block is hand-authored and must stay above "catalogs": scripts/build-5e-srd-catalogs.mjs rewrites the catalogs key and everything after it.

skills.$comment: Prepared spells, plus cantrips, which are cast without being prepared and are level 0 on this sheet.

catalogs.$comment: The SRD 5.1 monsters as opponents a fight reads. It writes no rows onto a sheet, so the sheet editor's picker never offers it, and every number in it is written in the keys the combat block declares. Generated by scripts/build-5e-srd-catalogs.mjs. Do not edit by hand. Source: Open5e srd-2014 data, https://github.com/open5e/open5e-api, data/v2/wizards-of-the-coast/srd-2014, commit 0e594c370b4daa9c8d8690979a58eab615afd6d5, licensed CC-BY-4.0 like SRD 5.1 itself.
catalogs.label: Creatures

combat.$comment: How a battle is FOUGHT by these rules, which is what a game on this ruleset plays on. Generated by scripts/build-5e-srd-catalogs.mjs: the threat scale below is MEASURED from the SRD creatures of each challenge rating. The battle block above is what a game without the combat director still uses; a fight never uses both.

attackRoll.$comment: 2014 rules: a natural 20 on an attack roll always hits and is a critical, and a natural 1 always misses. A critical rolls the damage dice twice.

distance.$comment: SRD 5.1, Playing on a Grid: "Each square on the grid represents 5 feet." Every distance in this ruleset is in feet, so one cell is five of them.
distance.label: ft

ranged.$comment: SRD 5.1, Range: "Your attack has disadvantage when your target is beyond normal range." Ranged Attacks in Close Combat: "You have disadvantage on a ranged attack roll if you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature who can see you and who isn't incapacitated." The Engine reads the second rule from the shooter's own neighbours and cannot ask whether that neighbour sees them.

cover.$comment: SRD 5.1, Cover: "A target with half cover has a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws." Three-quarters cover and total cover are not in the Engine yet, so every piece of covering ground here is half cover, and the bonus applies to the attack roll and not to a saving throw.

opportunity.$comment: SRD 5.1, Opportunity Attacks: "You can make an opportunity attack when a hostile creature that you can see moves out of your reach. To make the opportunity attack, you use your reaction." Taking it is automatic in this Engine, because nothing opens a reaction window yet.

abilities.$comment: Prepared spells, plus cantrips, which are cast without being prepared and are level 0 on this sheet. What each one does is the catalog entry's own mechanics.

Class features you picked, for the ones the SRD states in numbers, such as Second Wind. No toHit and no saveDifficulty: a class feature's own difficulty is not the spell save DC, and none of the entries this package ships rolls to hit or asks for a save.

conditions.$comment: Only the parts of each condition the closed effect list can say today. Charmed and deafened have no effect it can express, so they are left out and stay plain records on the sheet.

dying.$comment: Three successes stabilise and three failures kill, which is each track's own maximum. A natural 20 brings the character back up with one hit point and a natural 1 counts twice.

threat.$comment: The scale an opponent NOBODY WROTE is pulled onto. MEASURED from the SRD 5.1 creatures of each challenge rating: health is the lowest to the highest average hit points, defense and toHit are the median Armor Class and the median best attack bonus, damagePerRound is the lowest to the highest best round against one target, and saveDifficulty is the median of the difficulties those creatures' actions name. Damage is measured only from the creatures whose fighting is in their actions, because a spellcaster's printed attack is a dagger and an action this format could not hold is a trait a fight never rolls. A rating the SRD has no creature for, or none that can be measured for damage, takes the midpoint of its nearest neighbours. The caps and floors are then made monotone along the rating order, which is the one place this table is smoothed: a higher rating may never allow less than a lower one, and the numbers themselves are still the SRD creatures' own. This package's own bestiary is never clamped to it.
